## Does the minus sign belong to the base? {#zero}

Evaluate each expression for $x\ne 0$. Circle the base raised to zero before applying any sign or coefficient outside it.

$$(-2x)^0 \qquad -2x^0 \qquad -(2x)^0$$

<details name="zero-working">
<summary>Reminder</summary>

Use the brackets to identify the base. A non-zero base raised to zero has value one.

</details>

<details name="zero-working">
<summary>Check my working</summary>

From left to right: $(-2x)^0=1$; $-2x^0=-2(1)=-2$; $-(2x)^0=-(1)=-1$. The complete bases are $-2x$, $x$ and $2x$.

</details>

<details name="zero-working">
<summary>Try a similar question</summary>

Compare $(-5t)^0$ and $-5t^0$.

</details>

<details name="zero-working">
<summary>Check the retry</summary>

$(-5t)^0=1$, while $-5t^0=-5(1)=-5$.

</details>
